lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Seven unknown objects crossed restricted airspace over the White House, on three working radars.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: July 1952. Controller Edward Nugent, Washington National Airport, tracks seven targets fifteen miles out. No known aircraft nearby.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Technicians check his radar. It works. Pilot Casey Pierman sees lights matching the blips.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Then two Air Force fighters head for Washington, and every blip vanishes. When the jets leave, they return.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Two airport radars and Andrews Air Force Base all track the same target. It disappears from all three at once.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: President Truman's aide phones the Air Force. Then comes the biggest Pentagon press conference since the Second World War.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: The official answer: temperature inversions bent the radar.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: But Navy radar specialist Lieutenant Holcomb was in the room, and judged the inversion too weak.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: So were they a temperature inversion, or solid objects over the White House?
